text:
maria: heads up — I'm seeing a weird auth pattern after last night's KMS rewrap. A batch of embeddings calls are showing up in the audit as `chat.generate` and attributed to `system-service` instead of the original api key owner. :rotating_light:

aj: :eyes: can you paste the raw log line?

maria: sure — excerpt below (redacted):
```
2026-03-20T03:12:09Z audit.INFO request_id=abc123 user_id=system-service route=/v1/chat.generate model=gpt-embed-001 token_id=tok_XXXX action=ALLOW reason=scope_match
2026-03-20T03:12:09Z auth.DEBUG token_meta_lookup token_id=tok_XXXX meta_tags=null
```

maria: note `model=gpt-embed-001` but route is `chat.generate` and token_meta_lookup returned null for `route_scope` tag. before rotation we always saw `route_scope=embeddings`.

tyler: hmm. I pulled the authz service logs around the same window — there's a short gap where the token metadata cache returns 404, then a fallback path that attaches `system-service` when attribution missing. suspecting the KMS rewrap invalidated some metadata blobs or the metadata store migration skipped rebinds.

aj: timeline? ops-bot shows KMS rewrap completed at 03:10 UTC. auth-bot shows authz deploy at 03:08 with v2.4.1. could be a timing edge between rewrap and deploy.

ops-bot: KMS: key-rewrap job completed for region-us at 2026-03-20T03:10:13Z. all key versions rotated, legacy wrappers retired.

auth-bot: deploy: authz-service v2.4.1 -> v2.5.0 at 2026-03-20T03:08:41Z (canary 15%).

sara: possible impact: tokens that rely on KMS-wrapped metadata (route tags stored encrypted) might have had decryption fail if deploy read old KMS metadata. That would strip `route_scope` and cause fallback to broader permission or to `system-service`. We should treat this as privilege widening risk.

maria: confirmed ~42 distinct requests over 3 minutes. all embeddings traffic, but audited as chat and attributed differently. no malicious pattern seen, but this circumvents per-route allowlist.

tyler: quick repro idea: create a test api key with `route_scope=embeddings` (persisted encrypted in metadata), then trigger a key-rewrap job in staging while rolling authz. see if token_meta_lookup returns null. I can run that in staging now.

aj: mitigation for prod: 1) temporarily block any request where token_meta_lookup returns null (fail closed) 2) schedule immediate rebind of metadata entries (re-encrypt/refresh) 3) rotate service account tokens that rely on legacy wrappers.

sara: agree fail-closed for route enforcement until we confirm metadata integrity. ops, can we pause any further KMS rewrap jobs?

ops-bot: KMS: scheduled rewraps paused for region-us. existing rotation agents halted.

maria: I'm going to open an emergency PR to make authz fail-closed if `route_scope` missing for user tokens (allow system-service exemptions only if mTLS and service-account). will tag @tyler for staging repro and @aj for rollback plan.

tyler: started staging repro, will report within 20m.

aj: prepping rollback plan for authz deploy -> revert v2.5.0 can be done within 10m if needed. also prepping temporary denylist rule to block `chat.generate` when model == embed-models and token_meta null.

sara: i'll start a brief incident board and set severity low->medium until we confirm. cataloging affected audit lines and owners.

maria: thanks. quick note: long-term fix — don't bundle critical authz metadata with KMS-wrapped blobs that can be invalidated by key rotation; instead store a KMS-wrapped key and persist metadata in DB encrypted with that key id, plus a rotation-safe rebind flow. I'll add this to the postmortem.

aj: +1. can we also add an alert on `route_scope=null && auth.allow==true` in audit pipeline? that would've flagged this immediately.

maria: adding alert to runbook now.

tyler: repro completed in staging: when rewrap hits and authz reads old wrapper id, token_meta_lookup returns null for ~100ms; authz fallback path hit and assigned system account. pushing a minimal patch to change fallback to deny in staging.

maria: patch opened -> #PR 4021, tests included, trying canary.

sara: please tag me when canary metrics look good.

aj: if canary looks fine, plan is to deploy patch, then run metadata rebind job to refresh all token metas, and finally resume rewraps.

maria: final note — audit evidence saved in /mnt/audit/2026-03-20/embeddings_scope_strip.log and I'll sync with legal if customer-visible tokens affected.

tyler: thanks team — good catch.

maria: will post final incident summary in #incidents once resolved. :white_check_mark:
